There are two types of obstructions that may appear in $\chi_{n}$ : the appearance of $c_{0}^{+}c\tilde{c}\mathcal{O}_{i}$ would represent an order $\lambda^{n}$ contribution to the RG beta function that violates marginality, whereas the appearance of the “anti-ghost dilaton” operator $c_{0}^{+}(c\partial^{2}c-\tilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\tilde{c})$ would represent an order $\lambda^{n}$ shift of the central charge that violates criticality of the worldsheet theory.

### 3.4 The role of dilaton and central charge shift

For a noncompact CFT $\mathbb{A}$ , an exactly marginal deformation can deform the central charge. When embedded in the worldsheet CFT, a central charge deformation would violate criticality. In the SFT language, this corresponds to an obstruction to solving the SFT equation by a term proportional to the anti-ghost dilaton $c_{0}^{+}(c\partial^{2}c-\tilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\tilde{c})$ .

It is useful to illustrate this phenomenon in the example of the linear dilaton deformation. Let $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ be the linear dilaton CFT described by the scalar field $Y$ and the stress-energy tensor

$$ \displaystyle T=-{1\over 2}(\partial Y)^{2}+{{\beta}\over 2}\partial^{2}Y, $$

where $\beta$ is the background charge, and the central charge is $c_{{\mathbb{D}}_{\beta}}=1+3{\beta}^{2}$ .77 7 Our convention is such that $Y(z,\bar{z})Y(0)\sim-\log|z|^{2}$ , with $L_{1}\partial Y=\beta$ , and $L_{0}Y={{\beta}\over 2}$ . The worldsheet matter CFT is taken to the tensor product of $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ with an auxiliary CFT of central charge $26-c_{\mathbb{D}_{\beta}}$ .

An infinitesimal deformation of the background charge is represented by a string field

$$ \displaystyle\Psi=\epsilon\Theta+{\cal O}(\epsilon^{2}), $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\Theta={1\over 2}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c})Y+c_{0}^{+}(c\partial Y-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}Y) $$

satisfies

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}\Theta={\beta}c_{0}^{+}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}). $$

That is, $\Psi=\epsilon\Theta$ violates the first order string field equation by the aforementioned anti-ghost dilaton obstruction term, which reflects a shift of central charge of the linear dilaton CFT due to the background charge deformation.

Note that the expression (3.14) for $\Theta$ is not in the Siegel gauge. A BRST-equivalent Siegel gauge representative is $\Theta^{\prime}=b_{0}^{+}Q_{B}\chi$ , where $\chi$ obeys $L_{0}^{+}\chi=\Theta$ . One can verify that in the $\beta\to 0$ limit, $\Theta^{\prime}$ reduces to the more familiar expression for the vertex operator of a linear dilaton profile [30], $\Theta^{\prime}|_{\beta=0}=-2c\widetilde{c}Y\partial Y\bar{\partial}Y+(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c})Y$ . Indeed, such a deformation shifts the background charge of the linear dilaton CFT by $\Delta\beta=-2\epsilon$ , which leads to a first order shift of central charge by

$$ \displaystyle\Delta c=12{\beta}\epsilon. $$

While the deformation of the linear dilaton background charge by itself does not correspond to a SFT solution, we observe in (3.15) that the BRST cohomology of the anti-ghost dilaton is trivialized in the presence of the linear dilaton CFT. This motivates embedding the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ into a worldsheet CFT of the form

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{A}\otimes\mathbb{D}_{\beta}\otimes\mathbb{M}\otimes(bc{\rm~system}), $$

where the auxiliary CFT has central charge $26-c_{\mathbb{A}}-c_{\mathbb{D}_{\beta}}$ , and consider a string field solution

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{\lambda}\in\hat{\cal H}_{0}\subset{\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}\otimes{\cal H}_{\mathbb{D}_{\beta}}\otimes{\cal V}_{0}\otimes{\cal H}_{bc} $$

that corresponds to the deformed worldsheet CFT

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}\otimes\mathbb{D}_{\beta(\lambda)}\otimes\mathbb{M}\otimes(bc{\rm~system}), $$

where $c_{{\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}}$ may differ from $c_{\mathbb{A}}$ , but this is compensated by a deformation of the background charge of the linear dilaton sector to $\beta(\lambda)$ , so that $c_{{\mathbb{A}}_{\lambda}}+c_{\mathbb{D}_{\beta(\lambda)}}=c_{\mathbb{A}}+c_{\mathbb{D}_{\beta}}$ . In SFT description, starting with a first order string field of the form (3.9), a shift of the central charge of $\mathbb{A}$ which corresponds to an anti-ghost dilaton contribution on the RHS of (3.11) would require turning on a dilaton string field proportional to $\Theta$ (3.15) in $W_{n}$ .

A general string field solution of the form (3.18) may couple the linear dilaton sector nontrivially to $\mathbb{A}$ . For the purpose of analyzing $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ , we would like to ensure that the SFT solution corresponds to the factorized worldsheet theory of the form (3.19). In principle, this can be checked from the spectrum and amplitudes of the fluctuations around $\Psi_{\lambda}$ . A particularly simple diagnosis of a decoupled linear dilaton sector $\mathbb{D}_{\beta^{\prime}}$ is the existence of the shift current $j=\partial Y^{\prime}$ , which is an “almost Virasoro-primary” in that $j$ is annihilated by $L_{n\geq 2}$ but with $L_{1}j=\beta^{\prime}$ (and $L_{0}j=0$ ). In the SFT description, this corresponds to linearized fluctuation string field ${\cal J}_{\Psi}$ of ghost number 1 around the background solution $\Psi$ that obeys

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle Q_{\Psi}{\cal J}_{\Psi}=-\beta^{\prime}{\cal K}_{\Psi}. $$

where $Q_{\Psi}$ is the deformed BRST charge as defined in (2.25), and ${\cal K}_{\Psi}$ is the ghost number 2 string field that corresponds to a constant shift of the dilaton. In the undeformed background, ${\cal J}_{\Psi}$ and ${\cal K}_{\Psi}$ reduce to

$$ \displaystyle{\cal J}_{0}=c\partial Y-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}Y,~~~~{\cal K}_{0}={1\over 2}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}), $$

where ${\cal K}_{0}$ is also known as the ghost dilaton operator [30]. Further aspects of this analysis will be discussed in section 5.2.

## 4 SFT solution for short RG flows

The perturbative SFT solutions that describe marginal deformations, as outlined in the previous section, can be generalized to describe a slightly relevant deformation of the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ that generates a short RG flow to a new fixed point CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ [22]. Here, a renormalized coupling $\lambda$ can be identified with the expansion parameter used in constructing the string field $\Psi_{\lambda}$ , and the IR fixed point value of $\lambda$ will determined by the SFT equation.

Let us assume that the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ of interest admits a slightly relevant operator $\phi$ of weight $h=\widetilde{h}=1-\varepsilon$ , where $\varepsilon$ is a small parameter that also controls the length of the RG flow generated by $\phi$ , in the sense that a suitable renormalized coupling will be small at the RG fixed point. We will embed $\mathbb{A}$ into a worldsheet theory of the form (3.19), and denote by $\mathbb{P}^{+}_{\varepsilon}$ the projector from the space of string fields $\hat{\cal H}$ to a subspace on which $|L_{0}^{+}|\lesssim{\cal O}(\varepsilon)$ .

### 4.1 A perturbative SFT solution describing the RG fixed point

Working in the gauge

$$ \displaystyle b_{0}^{+}(1-\mathbb{P}^{+}_{\varepsilon})\Psi=0, $$

and writing

$$ \displaystyle\Psi=W+\Psi_{>},~~~~W\equiv\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\Psi,~~~\Psi_{>}\equiv(1-\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+})\Psi, $$

we can construct a solution by iteratively solve

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W=-\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\sum_{n\geq 2}{1\over n!}\left[(W+\Psi_{>})^{\otimes n}\right], \displaystyle\Psi_{>}=-{b_{0}^{+}\over L_{0}^{+}}(1-\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+})\sum_{n\geq 2}{1\over n!}\left[(W+\Psi_{>})^{\otimes n}\right]. $$

We can further eliminate $\Psi_{>}$ and write an equation for $W$ itself, of the form

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W=-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}[W^{\otimes 2}]+{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\Big[W\otimes\Big({b_{0}^{+}\over L_{0}^{+}}(1-\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+})[W^{\otimes 2}]\Big)\Big]-{1\over 6}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}[W^{\otimes 3}]+\cdots $$

To proceed, we consider a perturbative expansion

$$ \displaystyle W=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon^{n}W_{n}, $$

where $W_{1}$ takes the form of a first order deformation by the relevant operator $\phi$ ,

$$ \displaystyle W_{1}=g_{1}c\widetilde{c}\phi. $$

Note that $W_{1}$ is not BRST closed, since $\phi$ is not marginal. However, $Q_{B}W_{1}$ is of order $\varepsilon$ due to $\phi$ being nearly marginal,

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{1}=-2\varepsilon g_{1}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\phi. $$

The SFT equation (4.4) at order $\varepsilon^{2}$ gives

$$ \displaystyle-2\varepsilon^{2}g_{1}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\phi+\varepsilon^{2}Q_{B}W_{2}=-{\varepsilon^{2}g_{1}^{2}\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\left[c\widetilde{c}\phi\otimes c\widetilde{c}\phi\right]+{\cal O}(\varepsilon^{3}). $$

To carry out the explicit calculations, it will be convenient to work in the flat-vertex frame defined in section 2.4,88 8 The reader should be cautious that the string field solution in the flat-vertex frame, which solves the deformed SFT equation of the form (2.39), is related to the string field that appears in an action (necessarily constructed from symmetric vertices) by the field redefinition (2.38). in which the flat 2-string bracket (2.41) gives

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\left[c\widetilde{c}\phi\otimes c\widetilde{c}\phi\right] \displaystyle=b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}^{-}r_{0}^{-L_{0}^{+}}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}(c\widetilde{c}\phi(-z_{0})c\widetilde{c}\phi(z_{0})) \displaystyle=2\left({r_{0}\over 2|z_{0}|}\right)^{2\varepsilon}C_{\phi\phi\phi}\,c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\phi, $$

where $C_{\phi\phi\phi}$ is the structure constant appearing in the $\phi\phi$ OPE, assuming that $\phi$ is the only nearly marginal operator. With $W_{2}=g_{2}c\widetilde{c}\phi$ for some order one coefficient $g_{2}$ and thus $Q_{B}W_{2}={\cal O}(\varepsilon)$ , we can solve (4.8) by setting

$$ \displaystyle g_{1}={2\over C_{\phi\phi\phi}}. $$

Therefore, we have determine $W$ up to second order to be of the form

$$ \displaystyle W=\lambda c\widetilde{c}\phi+{\cal O}(\varepsilon^{3}),~~~~\lambda={2\varepsilon\over C_{\phi\phi\phi}}+{\cal O}(\varepsilon^{2}). $$

$\lambda$ can be viewed as a renormalized coupling at the RG fixed point. Note that in particular we have not invoked a term proportional to $\Theta$ (3.14) in the linear dilaton sector, indicating that there is no shift of central charge of the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ at order $\varepsilon^{2}$ .

### 4.2 Central charge shift at the third order

We seek an anti-ghost dilaton term of the form

$$ \displaystyle a\,c_{0}^{+}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}) $$

on the RHS of (4.4), which would require turning on a dilaton component of $W$ in the form ${\beta}^{-1}a\Theta$ , where $\Theta$ is given by (3.14), resulting in a shift of the central charge of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ by

$$ \displaystyle\Delta c\equiv c_{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}-c_{\mathbb{A}}=-12a. $$

At order $\varepsilon^{3}$ , the relevant terms on the RHS of (4.4) are99 9 There are also order $\varepsilon^{3}$ terms coming from $-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}[W_{1}^{\otimes 2}]$ , due to the $\varepsilon$ -dependence of (4.9), but these do not contain the anti-ghost dilaton.

$$ \displaystyle-\varepsilon^{3}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}[W_{1}\otimes W_{2}]+{\varepsilon^{3}\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\Big[W_{1}\otimes\Big({b_{0}^{+}\over L_{0}^{+}}(1-\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+})[W_{1}^{\otimes 2}]\Big)\Big]-{\varepsilon^{3}\over 6}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}[W_{1}^{\otimes 3}]. $$

Let $\sigma$ be the difference between the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic ghost numbers, e.g. $c$ carries $\sigma=1$ and $\widetilde{c}$ carries $\sigma=-1$ . $W_{1}$ and $W_{2}$ both have $\sigma=0$ . The 2-string bracket changes $\sigma$ by $\pm 1$ , however $b_{0}^{+}[W_{1}^{\otimes 2}]$ has $\sigma=0$ . Therefore, only the last term in (4.14) involving the 3-string bracket can contain an anti-ghost dilaton, which involves terms of $\sigma=\pm 3$ . We adopt an asymmetric flat 4-string vertex with coordinate maps

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle f_{1}(w_{1})=r_{0}w_{1}^{-1}, \displaystyle f_{2}(w_{2})=q_{1}w_{2}+z_{1}, \displaystyle f_{3}(w_{3})=q_{2}w_{3}+z_{2}, \displaystyle f_{4}(w_{4})=q_{3}w_{4}+z_{3}, $$

where $q_{i}=q_{i}(t,\bar{t})$ and $z_{i}=z_{i}(t,\bar{t})$ are suitably chosen functions of the complex modulus $t$ over a domain ${\cal D}_{4}\subset{\cal M}_{0,4}$ (Figure 3), such that on the three boundaries of the domain they match with the plumbing of a pair of flat 3-vertices modulo constant phase rotations of $w_{i}$ according to the geometric master equation. If we take $t$ to be the cross ratio $z_{31}/z_{21}$ , the 4-vertex domain is

$$ \displaystyle{\cal D}_{4}=\left\{t\in\mathbb{C}:~\left|t-{1\over 2}\right|,\left|{1\over t}-{1\over 2}\right|,\left|{1\over 1-t}-{1\over 2}\right|<r_{0}\right\}. $$

*Figure 3: The domain ${\cal D}_{4}$ in the moduli space ${\cal M}_{0,4}$ parameterized by the cross ratio $t$ , and corresponding 4-punctured sphere with the local charts of a flat 4-vertex.*

The matching condition on the boundary $t={1\over 2}+r_{0}e^{i\theta}$ for instance is

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle|q_{1}|=|q_{2}|={1\over r_{0}},~~~|q_{3}|=1, \displaystyle z_{1}=-z_{0}{t+{1\over 2}\over t-{1\over 2}},~~~z_{2}=-z_{0}{t-{3\over 2}\over t-{1\over 2}},~~~z_{3}=z_{0}. $$

The resulting flat 3-string bracket is

$$ \displaystyle={b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}^{-}\over(-2\pi i)}\int_{{\cal D}_{4}}dt\wedge d\bar{t}B_{t}B_{\bar{t}}\,(|q_{1}|^{L_{0}^{+}}\Psi)(z_{1})(|q_{2}|^{L_{0}^{+}}\Psi)(z_{2})(|q_{3}|^{L_{0}^{+}}\Psi)(z_{3}), $$

where

$$ \displaystyle B_{t}=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\left[b_{-1}^{(z_{i})}{\partial z_{i}\over\partial t}+b_{0}^{(z_{i})}q_{i}^{-1}{\partial q_{i}\over\partial t}+\widetilde{b}_{-1}^{(\bar{z}_{i})}{\partial\bar{z}_{i}\over\partial t}+\widetilde{b}_{0}^{(\bar{z}_{i})}\bar{q}_{i}^{-1}{\partial\bar{q}_{i}\over\partial t}\right]. $$

Here $b_{n}^{(z_{i})}$ stands for $b_{n}$ acting on the operator inserted at $z_{i}$ .

The anti-ghost dilaton coefficient at order $\varepsilon^{3}$ can now be evaluated as

$$ \displaystyle a \displaystyle={\varepsilon^{3}\over 6}b_{0}^{+}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}[W_{1}^{\otimes 3}]|_{\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}} \displaystyle=-{\varepsilon^{3}\over 6(2\pi i)}b_{0}^{+}b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}_{\varepsilon}^{+}\mathbb{P}^{-}\int_{{\cal D}_{4}}dt\wedge d\bar{t}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{3}b_{-1}^{(z_{i})}{\partial z_{i}\over\partial t}\right)\left(\sum_{j=1}^{3}b_{-1}^{(z_{j})}{\partial z_{j}\over\partial\bar{t}}\right)W_{1}(z_{1})W_{1}(z_{2})W_{1}(z_{3})\bigg|_{\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}} \displaystyle=-{\varepsilon^{3}g_{1}^{3}C_{\phi\phi\phi}\over 6(2\pi i)}\int_{{\cal D}_{4}}\omega, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\omega \displaystyle={z_{3}dz_{1}\wedge dz_{2}\over z_{12}z_{13}z_{23}}+{\rm cyclic}=d\zeta,~~~~\zeta={z_{1}+z_{2}+z_{3}\over 3}\left({dz_{1}\over z_{12}z_{13}}+{\rm cyclic}\right). $$

(4.20) is thus reduced to a boundary integral, which can be evaluated using the matching condition (4.17) to give

$$ \displaystyle a \displaystyle=-{\varepsilon^{3}g_{1}^{3}C_{\phi\phi\phi}\over 6(2\pi i)}\int_{\partial{\cal D}_{4}}\zeta \displaystyle=-{\varepsilon^{3}g_{1}^{3}C_{\phi\phi\phi}\over 6(2\pi i)}\cdot 3\int_{C_{\infty}}{(1-2t)dt\over 12t(t-1)} \displaystyle={1\over 12}\varepsilon^{3}g_{1}^{3}C_{\phi\phi\phi}. $$

Substituting the solution for $g_{1}$ (4.10) and using the relation (4.13), we find the central charge shift

$$ \displaystyle\Delta c=-{8\varepsilon^{3}\over C_{\phi\phi\phi}^{2}} $$

in agreement with [13, 22].

## 5 Recovering CFT data from SFT

### 5.1 CFT spectrum from string field fluctuations

To recover the CFT data of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ that corresponds to a given SFT solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ (3.6), we begin by considering string field fluctuations around $\Psi_{\lambda}$ of the form

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{h,\widetilde{h}}\in\hat{\cal H}_{h,\widetilde{h}}\subset{\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}\otimes{\cal V}_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}}\otimes{\cal H}_{bc}, $$

where ${\cal V}_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}}$ is the space of Virasoro descendants of the mock primary $\Upsilon_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}}$ in the auxiliary CFTs, and $\hat{\cal H}_{h,\widetilde{h}}$ is the subspace of ${\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}\otimes{\cal V}_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}}\otimes{\cal H}_{bc}$ annihilated by $b_{0}^{-}$ and $L_{0}^{-}$ . We seek solutions to the linearized SFT equation

$$ \displaystyle Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}\Phi_{h,\widetilde{h}}=0 $$

of ghost number 2, where $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ is the deformed BRST charge defined as in (2.25), that represent on-shell fluctuations, subject to the gauge redundancy $\Phi_{h,\widetilde{h}}\sim\Phi_{h,\widetilde{h}}+Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}\chi$ . Note that by construction $\Psi_{\lambda}$ does not involve non-identity primaries of the auxiliary CFT, and therefore the equation (5.2) does not involve any CFT data of the auxiliary CFT other than the assumed conformal weight of the mock primary.

The background independence of SFT (proven for infinitesimal deformations in [17, 18, 19, 20, 21]) would imply an isomorphism between the cohomology of $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ on $\hat{\cal H}_{h,\widetilde{h}}$ and the (undeformed) BRST cohomology of the deformed worldsheet CFT (3.5) restricted to the subspace of

$$ \displaystyle{\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}\otimes{\cal V}_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}}\otimes{\cal H}_{bc} $$

annihilated by $b_{0}^{-}$ and $L_{0}^{-}$ . In particular, the latter admits a nontrivial BRST representative of the form

$$ \displaystyle c\widetilde{c}\,{\bf\varphi}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}\Upsilon_{1-h,1-\widetilde{h}} $$

if $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ admits a primary ${\bf\varphi}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}$ of weight $(h,\widetilde{h})$ . There should be a corresponding $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ -cohomology represented by a solution to (5.2) of the form (5.1) with ghost number 2.

On the other hand, for a compact CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ , at generic $(h,\widetilde{h})$ there is no nontrivial BRST-cohomology in (5.3), and there should be no corresponding $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ -cohomology of the form (5.1). Therefore, by seeking nontrivial solutions to (5.2), which may be constructed in perturbation theory, we will be able to determine the possible weights $(h,\widetilde{h})$ of primaries of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ . The extraction of further CFT data such as correlation functions from the SFT approach will be discussed in section 5.3.

To proceed, we can expand $\Phi_{h,\widetilde{h}}$ on a basis of Virasoro descendants of the mock primary as

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{h(\lambda),\widetilde{h}(\lambda)}=\sum_{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}(\lambda){\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{N}}\widetilde{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{\widetilde{N}}}\Upsilon_{1-h(\lambda),1-\widetilde{h}(\lambda)}, $$

where ${\underline{N}}\equiv\{n_{1},\cdots,n_{k}\}$ is a sequence of non-negative integers in descending order, ${\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{N}}\equiv L_{-n_{1}}^{\mathbb{M}}\cdots L_{-n_{k}}^{\mathbb{M}}$ is a complete basis of descending operators of the $c=26-c_{\mathbb{A}}$ holomorphic Virasoro algebra of the auxiliary CFT $\mathbb{M}$ , and similarly for its anti-holomorphic counterpart $\widetilde{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{\widetilde{N}}}$ .1010 10 For simplicity, we will assume that the primary weights are generic so that there are no null descendants. We will also write $|N|\equiv n_{1}+\cdots+n_{k}$ for the level of the Virasoro descendant.

Note that in (5.5) we have explicitly indicated the dependence of the weights $(h(\lambda),\widetilde{h}(\lambda))$ on the deformation parameter $\lambda$ . Generally, we expect the spin $s=h(\lambda)-\widetilde{h}(\lambda)$ to be independent of $\lambda$ , whereas the scaling dimension $\Delta(\lambda)=h(\lambda)+\widetilde{h}(\lambda)$ is to be determined by solving the linearized SFT equation (5.2). $\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}(\lambda)\in{\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}\otimes{\cal H}_{bc}$ are subject to the initial condition at $\lambda=0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}(0)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}c\widetilde{c}\varphi,&|N|=|\widetilde{N}|=0\\
0,&|N|+|\widetilde{N}|\geq 1\end{array}\right. $$

where $\varphi$ is a primary of the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ with weight $(h_{\varphi},\widetilde{h}_{\varphi})=(h(0),\widetilde{h}(0))$ . Generally, when there are multiple primaries of $\mathbb{A}$ of the same weight, an operator-mixing problem must be solved to determine $\varphi$ as a suitable linear combination of a basis of degenerate primaries with $\lambda$ -dependent coefficients, as is standard in degenerate perturbation theory. For simplicity of discussion, we will proceed by assuming that such degeneracies are absent.

There are two equivalent methods of carrying out the perturbation analysis of the fluctuation spectrum. The first method is to directly expand $\Phi_{h(\lambda),\widetilde{h}(\lambda)}$ with respect to $\lambda$ . This requires formally taking derivatives with respect to the weight of the mock primary and would necessitate working in a larger formal space of states. The second method, which is more convenient for practical computations, is to first eliminate the mock primaries by reducing the linearized SFT equation to a set of equations for $\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}(\lambda)$ and $\Delta(\lambda)$ , which can then be solved perturbatively in $\lambda$ . We now demonstrate the latter approach at the leading nontrivial order.

Writing

$$ \displaystyle\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}(\lambda)=c\widetilde{c}\varphi\,\delta_{|N|+|\widetilde{N}|,0}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda^{n}\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}_{n}, $$

but keeping general $\lambda$ -dependence in $(h(\lambda),\widetilde{h}(\lambda))$ , we can expand the linearized SFT equation (5.2) in the background (3.8) as

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}c\widetilde{c}\varphi\Upsilon+\lambda Q_{B}\sum_{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}\Phi_{1}^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{N}}\widetilde{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{\widetilde{N}}}\Upsilon+\lambda\left[\Psi_{1}\otimes c\widetilde{c}\varphi\Upsilon\right]={\cal O}(\lambda^{2}), $$

where we have used the abbreviated notation $\Upsilon$ for $\Upsilon_{1-h(\lambda),1-\widetilde{(}\lambda)}$ . The notation “ ${\cal O}(\lambda^{2})$ ” on the RHS means states built out of Virasoro descendants of $\Upsilon$ with ${\cal O}(\lambda^{2})$ coefficients. Imposing the Siegel gauge condition $b_{0}^{+}\Phi^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}_{n}=0$ , we can act $b_{0}^{+}$ on (5.8) to obtain

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle(\Delta(0)-\Delta(\lambda))c\widetilde{c}\varphi\Upsilon+\lambda\sum_{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}((L_{0}^{\mathbb{A}})^{+}+(L_{0}^{\rm gh})^{+}+|N|+|\widetilde{N}|+2-\Delta(\lambda))\Phi_{1}^{\underline{N},\underline{\widetilde{N}}}{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{N}}\widetilde{\cal L}^{\mathbb{M}}_{-\underline{\widetilde{N}}}\Upsilon \displaystyle+\lambda b_{0}^{+}\left[\Psi_{1}\otimes c\widetilde{c}\varphi\Upsilon\right]={\cal O}(\lambda^{2}). $$

Using $\Psi_{1}=c\widetilde{c}{\cal O}$ (3.9), and working with the flat-vertex frame string field (as defined in section 2.4), we can write the $\mathbb{M}$ -level 0 component of (5.9) as

$$ \displaystyle(\Delta(0)-\Delta(\lambda))c\widetilde{c}\varphi+\lambda(L_{0}^{+}+2-\Delta(\lambda))\Phi_{1}^{\{\},\{\}} \displaystyle+\lambda b_{0}^{+}b_{0}^{-}r_{0}^{-L_{0}^{+}-2+\Delta(\lambda)}\left(c\widetilde{c}{\cal O}(-z_{0})c\widetilde{c}\varphi(z_{0})\right)|_{L_{0}^{-}=s}={\cal O}(\lambda^{2}), $$

where in the third term, the restriction to the spin $L_{0}^{-}=s$ component comes from stripping off $\Upsilon$ followed by the spin projection $\mathbb{P}^{-}$ . Further projecting onto the ghost sector ground state, we have

$$ \displaystyle(\Delta(0)-\Delta(\lambda))\varphi+\lambda(L_{0}^{+}-\Delta(\lambda))\Phi_{1}^{\{\},\{\}}|_{c\widetilde{c}}+2\lambda r_{0}^{\Delta(\lambda)-L_{0}^{+}}|2z_{0}|^{2}\left({\cal O}(-z_{0})\varphi(z_{0})\right)|_{L_{0}^{-}=s}={\cal O}(\lambda^{2}) $$

as an equation in ${\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}$ . Due to the freedom of overall rescaling of the fluctuation string field $\Phi$ , we can assume without loss of generality that $\Phi_{1}^{\{\},\{\}}|_{c\widetilde{c}}$ is orthogonal to $\varphi$ . Further assuming that $\varphi$ is the only primary in ${\cal H}_{\mathbb{A}}$ of weight $(h_{\varphi},\widetilde{h}_{\varphi})$ , $h_{\varphi}-\widetilde{h}_{\varphi}=s$ , taking the overlap of (5.11) with $\varphi$ then determines1111 11 Here $\bar{\varphi}$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\varphi$ , and we have normalized $\langle\varphi\bar{\varphi}\rangle=1$ , assuming that the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ is compact.

$$ \displaystyle\Delta(\lambda)=\Delta(0)+2\lambda C_{{\cal O}\varphi\bar{\varphi}}+{\cal O}(\lambda^{2}), $$

in agreement with the result of first order conformal perturbation theory.

### 5.2 Decoupling the linear dilaton sector

To study deformations of CFTs that change the central charge, as discussed in section 3.4, we replace $\mathbb{A}$ by its tensor product with a linear dilaton CFT $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ . To ensure that the string field solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ corresponds to a deformed worldsheet CFT of the factorized form (3.19), a criterion (3.20) for the decoupling of the linear dilaton sector was introduced, which we now analyze in more detail.

The ghost dilaton ${\cal K}_{0}$ (3.21) can be written as

$$ \displaystyle{\cal K}_{0}=Q_{B}\varkappa, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\varkappa\equiv{1\over 2}(\partial c-\bar{\partial}\widetilde{c})=c_{0}^{-}\cdot 1, $$

is not a closed string field since it is not annihilated by $b_{0}^{-}$ . This can be generalized to an expression for the string field that describes a constant dilaton shift around a nontrivial background solution $\Psi$ [30], of the form

$$ \displaystyle{\cal K}_{\Psi}=Q_{B}\varkappa-\Psi+[\Psi\otimes\varkappa]+\cdots, $$

where $\cdots$ stands for higher order terms in $\Psi$ . The full expression of ${\cal K}_{\Psi}$ is given by the Hamiltonian vector field defined by (4.8) and (8.3) of [30], shifted by $-\Psi$ due to our normalization of the string field (such that the string coupling drops out of the equation of motion), which can be further transformed into the flat-vertex frame according to the prescription of section 2.4. The decoupling criterion (3.20) seeks to trivialize ${\cal K}_{\Psi}$ through a ghost number 1 string field ${\cal J}_{\Psi}$ that corresponds to the shift symmetry in the linear dilaton direction.

In the example of SFT solution describing a short RG flow of section 4.2, we have seen that a nontrivial dilaton profile is turned on at order $\lambda^{3}$ , and therefore at the next order in $\lambda$ the SFT solution will necessarily involve products of non-identity primaries from both $\mathbb{A}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ , potentially leading to a cohomological obstruction for solving (3.20), namely

$$ \displaystyle Q_{\Psi}{\cal J}_{\Psi}+{\beta}^{\prime}{\cal K}_{\Psi}=R_{\Psi} $$

is an order $\lambda^{4}$ string field that represents a nontrivial $Q_{\Psi}$ -cohomology. We can remove this obstruction by correcting the SFT solution $\Psi$ to $\Psi+\Delta\Psi$ , where $\Delta\Psi$ satisfies

$$ \displaystyle{}\left[\Delta\Psi\otimes{\cal J}_{0}\right]+{\beta}^{\prime}(-\Delta\Psi+[\Delta\Psi\otimes\varkappa])=R_{\Psi}+({\rm higher~order}). $$

Such a procedure allows for constructing a solution that satisfies the decoupling criterion (3.20) order by order in $\lambda$ , as desired.

### 5.3 CFT correlators from string amplitudes

The correlation functions of the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ can be extracted from the on-shell string amplitudes in the background (3.5), which are reproduced in the SFT as the tree-level amplitudes of on-shell fluctuations around the solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ . For this purpose, it is necessary to consider the SFT action functional, given by [16]

$$ \displaystyle S[\Psi]={1\over 2}\langle\Psi|c_{0}^{-}Q_{B}|\Psi\rangle+\sum_{n=3}^{\infty}{1\over n!}\{\Psi^{\otimes n}\}, $$

where $\langle\cdot|$ stands for BPZ conjugate, and $\{\cdots\}$ stands for symmetric string vertices that obey the BV master equation (2.17). The variational principle of (2.17) leads to the equation of motion (2.23).

In the Siegel gauge $b_{0}^{+}\Psi=0$ , using $\{Q_{B},b_{0}^{+}\}=L_{0}^{+}$ one can write the kinetic term as

$$ \displaystyle{1\over 2}\langle\Psi|c_{0}^{-}Q_{B}|\Psi\rangle={1\over 2}\langle\Psi|c_{0}^{-}c_{0}^{+}L_{0}^{+}|\Psi\rangle, $$

giving rise to a propagator proportional to $1/L_{0}^{+}$ . The $n$ -point tree-amplitude of on-shell linearized fluctuations $\Phi_{1},\cdots,\Phi_{n}\in\hat{\cal H}$ that obey $b_{0}^{+}\Phi_{i}=Q_{B}\Phi_{i}=0$ can be turned into a single integral over ${\cal M}_{0,n}$ in the familiar form

$$ \displaystyle{\cal A}_{\mathbb{A}}(\Phi_{1},\ldots,\Phi_{n})=\frac{1}{(-2\pi i)^{n-3}}\int_{{\cal M}_{0,n}}\left\langle\prod_{k=1}^{2n-6}\mathcal{B}_{k}dt^{k}\prod_{i=1}^{n}\Phi_{i}\right\rangle_{\mathbb{A}\otimes\mathbb{M}\otimes(bc)}. $$

In particular, if we take

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{i}=c\widetilde{c}\varphi_{i}\Upsilon_{1-h_{i},1-\widetilde{h}_{i}}, $$

where $\varphi_{i}$ is a primary of $\mathbb{A}$ of weight $(h_{i},\widetilde{h}_{i})$ , the integrand is determined via Virasoro Ward identities by the $n$ -point function $\langle\varphi_{1}\cdots\varphi_{n}\rangle_{\mathbb{A}}$ in the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ and the $n$ -point function of mock primaries

$$ \displaystyle f(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n})\equiv\left\langle\prod_{i=1}^{n}\Upsilon_{1-h_{i},1-\widetilde{h}_{i}}(z_{i})\right\rangle_{\mathbb{M}} $$

in the auxiliary CFT $\mathbb{M}$ .

The SFT amplitude prescription can be straightforwardly extended to the nontrivial background solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ , via the action

$$ \displaystyle S_{\Psi_{\lambda}}[\Psi^{\prime}] \displaystyle\equiv S[\Psi_{\lambda}+\Psi^{\prime}]-S[\Psi_{\lambda}] \displaystyle={1\over 2}\langle\Psi^{\prime}|c_{0}^{-}Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}|\Psi^{\prime}\rangle+\sum_{m\geq 0,n\geq 3}{1\over m!n!}\{\Psi_{\lambda}^{\otimes m}\otimes\Psi^{\prime\otimes n}\}. $$

The $n$ -point tree amplitudes of the on-shell fluctuations $\Phi_{i}\in\hat{\cal H}_{h_{i},\widetilde{h}_{i}}$ , $i=1,\cdots,n$ , that obey $b_{0}^{+}\Phi_{i}=Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}\Phi_{i}=0$ , will be denoted1212 12 See [16, 31] for a detailed description of the Feynman rules based on the SFT action.

$$ \displaystyle{\cal A}_{\mathbb{A}}(\Phi_{1},\cdots,\Phi_{n}|\Psi_{\lambda}). $$

Note that (5.24) depends on the auxiliary CFT data only through the $n$ -function of mock primaries $f(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n})$ (5.22), as $\Psi_{\lambda}$ does not involve non-identity mock primaries.

Suppose the $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ -cohomology of $\Phi_{i}$ corresponds to the on-shell vertex operator

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{i}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}=c\widetilde{c}\varphi_{i}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}\Upsilon_{1-h_{i},1-\widetilde{h}_{i}} $$

in the deformed worldsheet CFT (3.5) in the manner described in section 5.1, then the amplitude (5.24) should admit an equivalent expression

$$ \displaystyle{\cal A}_{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}(\Phi_{1}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}},\cdots,\Phi_{n}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}) $$

defined as in (5.20) except that the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ is replaced by $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ . In particular, (5.26) is expressed as a integral over ${\cal M}_{0,n}$ , whose integrand is determined via Virasoro Ward identities by the $n$ -point function $\langle\varphi_{1}\cdots\varphi_{n}\rangle_{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}$ in the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ , and the same $n$ -point function of mock primaries $f(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n})$ as appearing in (5.24).

Equating (5.26) with (5.24) and considering functional variations with respect to $f(z_{1},\cdots,z_{n})$ then in principle determines the correlation functions of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ in terms of the CFT data of $\mathbb{A}$ . In particular, the structure constants of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ are given by1313 13 Here it is important that one works with symmetric string vertices. A solution of the deformed string field equation (2.39) defined via the asymmetric flat vertices of section 2.4 would be related to $\Psi_{\lambda}$ appearing in (5.27) by a field redefinition obtained by integrating (2.38).

$$ \displaystyle C_{ijk}^{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}} \displaystyle={\cal A}_{\mathbb{A}}(\Phi_{i},\Phi_{j},\Phi_{k}|\Psi_{\lambda}) \displaystyle=\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}{1\over m!}\{\Psi_{\lambda}^{\otimes m}\otimes\Phi_{i}\otimes\Phi_{j}\otimes\Phi_{k}\}, $$

where the 3-point function coefficient of mock primaries appearing on the RHS is normalized to 1. This formula amounts to a precise all-order implementation of renormalized conformal perturbation theory. The background solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ plays the role of a Wilsonian effective action at the RG fixed point. The choice of string vertices, subject to the geometric master equation (2.12), is analogous to a renormalization scheme. The dependence on the choice of string vertices can be absorbed by a string field redefinition, and drops out of the on-shell amplitude. The latter relies crucially on the $Q_{\Psi_{\lambda}}$ -closure of $\Phi_{i},\Phi_{j},\Phi_{k}$ . Furthermore, the SFT amplitude on the RHS of (5.27) is manifestly finite, where the moduli integrations appearing in the string vertices by construction avoid the boundary of the moduli space where operators would collide.

## 6 Application I: the Horowitz-Polchinski solution

Consider the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ given by $d$ noncompact free bosons $\vec{Z}=(Z^{1},\cdots,Z^{d})$ together with a compact boson $X$ at radius $R={1\over\sqrt{2}}$ (i.e. half of the self-dual radius1414 14 As in section 3.4, we work in ${\alpha}^{\prime}=2$ convention.), and a string field of the form

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle\Psi_{\lambda}=W_{\lambda}+(1-\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{+})\Psi_{\lambda}, \displaystyle W_{\lambda}=\lambda\Big[c\widetilde{c}f(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})\cos(\sqrt{2}X)+c\widetilde{c}g(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})\partial X\bar{\partial}X\Big]+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

where $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{+}$ stands for the projector onto states with $|L_{0}^{+}|\lesssim{\cal O}(\lambda)$ , and $f,g$ are smooth and bounded spherically symmetric functions on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Importantly, we will keep track of the $\lambda$ dependence of $f(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})$ and $g(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})$ in the region of large $|\vec{Z}|$ in the field target space, while omitting higher order corrections that are suppressed by powers of $\lambda$ globally in the target space.

As in (4.4), the SFT equation for $\Psi_{\lambda}$ can be brought to the form

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{\lambda}+{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{+}[W_{\lambda}^{\otimes 2}]={\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

The ansatz (6.1) gives

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{\lambda}=\lambda^{2}c_{0}^{+}\Big[c\widetilde{c}(-\nabla^{2}f)(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})\cos(\sqrt{2}X)+c\widetilde{c}(-\nabla^{2}g)(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})\partial X\bar{\partial}X\Big]+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

and with the 2-string bracket in the flat-vertex frame,

$$ \displaystyle{}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{+}[W_{\lambda}^{\otimes 2}] \displaystyle=b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}^{-}r_{0}^{-L_{0}^{+}}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}^{+}(W_{\lambda}(-z_{0})W_{\lambda}(z_{0})) \displaystyle=\lambda^{2}2c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\left[-2f(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})g(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z})\cos(\sqrt{2}X)-(f(\sqrt{\lambda}\vec{Z}))^{2}\partial X\bar{\partial}X\right]+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

Note that in particular, various terms in the $W_{\lambda}(-z_{0})W_{\lambda}(z_{0})$ OPE that involve the gradient of $f$ and $g$ are of order $\lambda^{3}$ .

Therefore, the SFT equation is satisfied up to ${\cal O}(\lambda^{3})$ terms provided

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle\nabla^{2}f+2fg=0, \displaystyle\nabla^{2}g+f^{2}=0. $$

These are precisely equations (2.7), (2.8) of [32] up to a simple rescaling and constant shift. For $d=3,4,5$ , a smooth, bounded, spherically symmetric solution to (6.5) exists, with the asymptotic behavior

$$ \displaystyle f(\infty)=0,~~~~g(\infty)\equiv g_{\infty}<0. $$

The string field (6.1) with $f,g$ satisfying (6.5) and (6.6) describes none other than the T-dual of the Horowitz-Polchinski “string star” [27].

In contrast to the analysis of [27, 32] which is based on massless effective field theory in $d$ dimensions, here we have given a first principle construction of the corresponding solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ in the classical bosonic closed SFT in a self-consistent weak field approximation, which can nonetheless be systematically improved by computing higher order corrections in $\lambda$ .1515 15 The effective field theory with quartic interaction has been analyzed in [33]. From the worldsheet conformal perturbation theory perspective, the smoothness of the functions $f$ and $g$ at the origin in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ may come as a surprise; it signifies that the string field captures renormalized rather than bare couplings.

## 7 Application II: tachyon-dilaton eschatology via Runkel-Watts walls

Let the CFT $\mathbb{A}$ be the $c=1$ free noncompact boson, and consider its deformation by the weight $(1,1)$ primary $\cos(\sqrt{2}X)$ . It is well known that the analogous deformation in a compact boson theory would not be exactly marginal [34], as a nonzero beta function would be generated at second order in conformal perturbation theory. In the noncompact setting, however, it is possible to correct the deformation at each order in the coupling to cancel the beta function at the price of breaking discrete shift symmetry in $X$ , so as to preserve marginality to all orders in perturbation theory. We will investigate such a perturbatively marginal deformation using the SFT approach by embedding $\mathbb{A}$ into the worldsheet CFT along with a linear dilaton sector $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ , as introduced in section 3.4. From the SFT perspective, the deformation amounts to turning on a closed string tachyon profile that varies in one spatial dimension, and we will analyze the fate of such a tachyon solution with nonlinear effects taken into account.

### 7.1 The perturbative SFT solution up to second order

We begin by seeking a SFT solution $\Psi_{\lambda}$ of the perturbative form (3.8) with the first order string field

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{1}=\lambda c\widetilde{c}\cos(\sqrt{2}X). $$

Following the strategy of section 3.3, we can write the second order string field solution as

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{2}=W_{2}-{1\over 2}{b_{0}^{+}\over L_{0}^{+}}(1-\mathbb{P}^{+})[\Psi_{1}^{\otimes 2}], $$

where $W_{2}$ is a weight $(0,0)$ string field that obeys

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{2}=-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}^{+}[\Psi_{1}^{\otimes 2}]=c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\partial X\bar{\partial}X. $$

In the absence of the linear dilaton sector $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ , the RHS of (7.3) would in fact represent a nontrivial $Q_{B}$ -cohomology class of ghost number 3 that obstructs the second order SFT solution, corresponding to a central charge shift of the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ at order $\lambda^{2}$ . This is mostly easily understood by rewriting (7.3) as

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{2}=c_{0}^{+}D_{X}+{1\over 2}c_{0}^{+}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c}), $$

where $D_{X}=c\widetilde{c}\partial X\bar{\partial}X-{1\over 2}(c\partial^{2}c-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}^{2}\widetilde{c})$ is the zero momentum limit of the vertex operator that corresponds to a dilaton profile in the $X$ direction [30]. Using the formula

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}(f(X)D_{X})=-c_{0}^{+}f^{\prime\prime}(X)D_{X}, $$

we can solve

$$ \displaystyle W_{2}=-{1\over 2}X^{2}D_{X}+{1\over 2{\beta}}\Theta, $$

where $\Theta$ is the string field that describes a shift of the background charge of $\mathbb{D}_{\beta}$ as defined in (3.14). In the notation of (4.12), (4.13), we have the anti-ghost dilaton coefficient $a={1\over 2}\lambda^{2}$ from (7.4), and thus a second order shift of the central charge of the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle c_{\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}}=1-6\lambda^{2}+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

The decoupling of the extraneous $Y$ -linear dilaton sector is manifest in (7.6). Starting at order $\lambda^{3}$ , it will be necessary to constrain the solution so as to maintain the decoupling as discussed in section 5.2.

### 7.2 Extending the solution to large field region

We observe that (7.6) describes a dilaton profile in $X$ direction of the form $\phi\sim{1\over 2}\lambda^{2}X^{2}$ , which is slowly varying at small $\lambda$ but grows with $X$ . By analogy with the Horowitz-Polchinski solution considered in section 6, we postulate the following ansatz that capture the slow-varying components of the string field at small $\lambda$ ,

$$ \displaystyle W_{\lambda}\equiv\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\Psi_{\lambda} \displaystyle={\lambda\over 2}c\widetilde{c}\left(f(\lambda X)e^{i\sqrt{2}X}+\bar{f}(\lambda X)e^{-i\sqrt{2}X}\right)+\phi(\lambda X){\cal K}_{0} \displaystyle+\lambda A(\lambda X)c_{0}^{+}(c\partial X-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}X)+c\widetilde{c}\,h(\lambda X)\partial X\bar{\partial}X+{\lambda^{2}\over 2\beta}\Theta+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

where $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}$ stands for the projection onto states with $|L_{0}^{+}|\lesssim{\cal O}(\lambda^{2})$ , ${\cal K}_{0}$ is the ghost dilaton defined in (3.21), $\Theta$ is defined in (3.14), and $f(x),\phi(x),A(x),h(x)$ are smooth functions of $x$ .1616 16 The functions $f(x),\phi(x),A(x),h(x)$ themselves may depend on $\lambda$ analytically, but this won’t affect the analysis of the SFT solution at the order we consider below.

On the RHS of (7.8) we have included all possible ghost number 2 string fields with $|L_{0}^{+}|\lesssim{\cal O}(\lambda^{2})$ that are even with respect to worldsheet parity1717 17 Note that by convention $c\widetilde{c}$ is parity even whereas the identity operator is parity odd. while maintaining the decoupling of the $Y$ -linear dilaton sector, the only assumption being the $\lambda$ -scaling which will be justified by solving the SFT equation below. The functions $f,\phi,A,h$ are not necessarily bounded, and the separation of these slow-varying fields from the higher order corrections in $\lambda$ is meaningful for the range of $X$ of order $\sim 1/\lambda$ . Note that we have not assumed the Siegel gauge condition in (7.8); as already seen in section 3.4, this will allow for the flexibility of making other more convenient gauge choices in computing the solution.

A priori, the appearance of $\phi(\lambda X)$ and $h(\lambda X)$ in (7.8) which are of order one would mean that all higher-point string vertices would contribute to the SFT equation that governs $W_{\lambda}$ . However, this complication can be evaded as follows. Firstly, we will work in a gauge in which

$$ \displaystyle h(\lambda X)=0. $$

Note that by doing so, we no longer have the freedom of gauging away $A(\lambda X)$ in (7.8). Secondly, we will work in the flat-vertex frame defined in section 2.4, in which the flat string bracket can never reduce the number of derivatives in a $\partial^{2}c$ appearing in a string field, and consequently the string bracket contributing to the equation of motion for $W_{\lambda}$ can never involve more than one insertion of $\phi(\lambda X){\cal K}_{0}$ . This is a major simplification that allows us to write down the full equation for (7.8) in the flat-vertex frame using only 2-string brackets.

Splitting the $X$ -dependent part of (7.8) into the “tachyon component”

$$ \displaystyle W_{T}={\lambda\over 2}c\widetilde{c}\left(f(\lambda X)e^{i\sqrt{2}X}+\bar{f}(\lambda X)e^{-i\sqrt{2}X}\right) $$

and the “dilaton component”

$$ \displaystyle W_{D}=\phi(\lambda X){\cal K}_{0}+\lambda A(\lambda X)c_{0}^{+}(c\partial X-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}X)+c\widetilde{c}\,h(\lambda X)\partial X\bar{\partial}X, $$

we can reduce the SFT equation, in the form of (4.4), to

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{T}=-\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{T}\otimes W_{D}]+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{D}=-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{T}^{\otimes 2}]-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{D}^{\otimes 2}]-\lambda^{2}c_{0}^{+}{\cal K}_{0}+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

On the LHS of (7.12), the BRST variations of $W_{T}$ and $W_{D}$ are computed from (7.10) and (7.11), up to higher order terms in $\lambda$ , as

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{T}=\sqrt{2}\lambda^{2}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}(-if^{\prime}(\lambda X)e^{i\sqrt{2}X}+i\bar{f}^{\prime}(\lambda X)e^{-i\sqrt{2}X})+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), \displaystyle Q_{B}W_{D}=-\lambda^{2}(\phi^{\prime\prime}(\lambda X)+A^{\prime}(\lambda X))c_{0}^{+}{\cal K}_{0}+\lambda(\phi^{\prime}(\lambda X)-A(\lambda X))(c\partial X+\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}X){\cal K}_{0} \displaystyle+2\lambda^{2}A^{\prime}(\lambda X)c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\partial X\bar{\partial}X+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

The projected 2-string brackets appearing on the RHS of (7.12) are computed, in the flat-vertex frame,1818 18 Note that with a non-flat string vertex, there would be additional terms on the RHS, particularly those that involve $\phi(\lambda X)$ . as

$$ \displaystyle-\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{T}\otimes W_{D}]=\sqrt{2}\lambda^{2}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}(-if(\lambda X)A(\lambda X)e^{i\sqrt{2}X}+i\bar{f}(\lambda X)A(\lambda X)e^{i\sqrt{2}X})+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), \displaystyle-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{T}^{\otimes 2}]=\lambda^{2}|f(\lambda X)|^{2}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\partial X\bar{\partial}X+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), \displaystyle-{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{D}^{\otimes 2}]=-2\lambda^{2}(\phi^{\prime}(\lambda X))^{2}c_{0}^{+}{\cal K}_{0}+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

Up to order $\lambda^{2}$ , (7.12) is thus reduced to the differential equations

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle A(x)=\phi^{\prime}(x), \displaystyle f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)A(x), \displaystyle A^{\prime}(x)={1\over 2}|f(x)|^{2}, \displaystyle\phi^{\prime\prime}(x)+A^{\prime}(x)=2(\phi^{\prime}(x))^{2}+1. $$

After eliminating $A(x)$ with the first equation of (7.15), we can solve the second equation of (7.15) with

$$ \displaystyle f(x)=e^{\phi(x)-\phi_{0}}, $$

where $\phi_{0}=\phi(0)$ by the normalization convention $f(0)=1$ . The remaining equations of (7.15) can now be expressed as

$$ \displaystyle\phi^{\prime\prime}(x)=(\phi^{\prime}(x))^{2}+{1\over 2}={1\over 2}e^{2\phi(x)-2\phi_{0}}, $$

where the first equality is in fact redundant, and we can solve the first order differential equation for $\phi$ to give

$$ \displaystyle\phi(x)=\phi_{0}-\log\big(\cos{x\over\sqrt{2}}\big). $$

The resulting solution of the projected string field (7.8), in the $h=0$ gauge and in the flat-vertex frame, is

$$ \displaystyle W_{\lambda}=\lambda c\widetilde{c}\,{\cos(\sqrt{2}X)\over\cos({\lambda X\over\sqrt{2}})}+\Big(\phi_{0}-\log\big(\!\cos{\lambda X\over\sqrt{2}}\big)\Big){\cal K}_{0}+{\lambda\over\sqrt{2}}\tan\!\big({\lambda X\over\sqrt{2}}\big)c_{0}^{+}(c\partial X-\widetilde{c}\bar{\partial}X)+{\lambda^{2}\over 2\beta}\Theta+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

From the target space perspective, this describes a string background with a weak tachyon field of spatial momentum $p\simeq\pm{1\over\sqrt{2}}$ whose amplitude $\lambda f(\lambda X)$ is further modulated over distance scale $1/\lambda$ , and a dilaton profile $\phi(\lambda X)$ that grows with increasing $|X|$ . Conspicuously, the dilaton diverges at

$$ \displaystyle X=\pm{\pi\over\sqrt{2}\lambda}+{\cal O}(\lambda^{0}), $$

and thus (7.19) is expected to be valid only in the regime ${\pi\over\sqrt{2}\lambda}\lesssim X\lesssim{\pi\over\sqrt{2}\lambda}$ , and describes a deformed background of finite space with walls at $|X|\approx{\pi\over\sqrt{2}\lambda}$ .

### 7.3 Runkel-Watts walls and the emergence of minimal model

Following the strategy outlined in section 5.1, we can analyze the low-lying spectrum of the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ by considering a linearized string field fluctuation $\Phi$ over the background solution (7.19) of the general form (5.1), with

$$ \displaystyle\Omega\equiv\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\Phi=c\widetilde{c}\,\xi(\lambda X)\Upsilon+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

where $\Upsilon$ is a mock primary of weight $(1-{\Delta\over 2},1-{\Delta\over 2})$ in the auxiliary CFT on the worldsheet, with

$$ \displaystyle\Delta=\lambda^{2}\gamma+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

and $\xi(\lambda X)$ is a wave function of wave length $\sim 1/\lambda$ to be determined. The linearized SFT equation can be put in the form

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}\Omega+\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{\lambda}\otimes\Omega\right]+{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{\lambda}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}={\cal O}(\lambda^{3}), $$

where we have defined the symmetric tri-linear map $[\cdot]^{\cal A}:\otimes\hat{\cal H}^{\otimes 3}\to\hat{\cal H}$ with

$$ \displaystyle\left[\Psi^{\otimes 3}\right]^{\cal A}\equiv[\Psi^{\otimes 3}]+3\big[{b_{0}^{+}\over L_{0}^{+}}(1-\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+})[\Psi^{\otimes 2}]\otimes\Psi\big]. $$

Working with the flat string bracket which cannot reduce the number of derivatives on $\partial^{2}c$ , we need not be concerned with the $\phi(\lambda X){\cal K}_{0}$ term in $W_{\lambda}$ (7.8), and thus can treat $W_{\lambda}$ as of order $\lambda$ in (7.23) and furthermore reduce (7.23) to

$$ \displaystyle Q_{B}\Omega+\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{D}\otimes\Omega\right]+{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{T}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}+{1\over 2}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{D}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}={\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

The first two terms in (7.23) are evaluated as

$$ \displaystyle \displaystyle Q_{B}\Omega=\lambda^{2}(-\xi^{\prime\prime}(\lambda X)-\gamma\xi(\lambda X))c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}\Upsilon+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}) \displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}[W_{D}\otimes\Omega]=2\lambda^{2}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}A(\lambda X)\xi^{\prime}(\lambda X)\Upsilon+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

The remaining terms can be evaluated as in a naive computation of a 4-point on-shell amplitude, but with suitable divergences subtracted. Relying crucially on simplifications due to the flat string bracket, we find that both $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{T}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}$ and $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{D}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}$ vanish up to ${\cal O}(\lambda^{3})$ terms.1919 19 $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{T}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}$ is computed by $\displaystyle{\lambda^{2}\over 2}{b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}^{-}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\over(-2\pi i)}\int^{\prime}_{{\cal M}_{0,4}}dt\wedge d\bar{t}B_{t}B_{\bar{t}}{c\widetilde{c}(z_{1})c\widetilde{c}(z_{2})c\widetilde{c}(z_{3})\over|z_{12}|^{4}}|f|^{2}\xi\Upsilon={\lambda^{2}\over 2\pi i}c_{0}^{+}c\widetilde{c}|f|^{2}\xi\Upsilon\int_{{\cal M}_{0,4}}^{\prime}\left|{z_{23}dz_{1}+z_{31}dz_{2}+z_{12}dz_{3}\over z_{12}^{2}}\right|^{2}$ (7.27) up to ${\cal O}(\lambda^{3})$ terms, where $z_{1},z_{2},z_{3}$ are functions of the moduli $t,\bar{t}$ as defined in (4.15), and the integration is over the entire moduli space ${\cal M}_{0,4}$ but subtracting the divergent powers of $z_{12}$ as $z_{12}\to 0$ while fixing $z_{3}$ and ${z_{1}+z_{2}\over 2}$ . Note that this manipulation is only valid for flat string brackets. Writing the integrand in the second line of (7.27) as $\left|d\big({z_{3}-{z_{1}+z_{2}\over 2}\over z_{12}}\big)\right|^{2}$ , one immediately sees that the result vanishes after subtracting divergences. $\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\left[W_{D}^{\otimes 2}\otimes\Omega\right]^{\cal A}$ is computed by $\displaystyle 2{\lambda^{2}}{b_{0}^{-}\mathbb{P}^{-}\mathbb{P}_{\lambda^{2}}^{+}\over(-2\pi i)}\int^{\prime}_{{\cal M}_{0,4}}dt\wedge d\bar{t}B_{t}B_{\bar{t}}{c_{0}^{+}c(z_{1})c_{0}^{+}c(z_{2})c\widetilde{c}(z_{3})\over z_{12}^{2}}A^{2}\xi\Upsilon$ (7.28) up to ${\cal O}(\lambda^{3})$ terms, which can only receive contributions from $(b_{0}^{+})^{(z_{i})}b_{-1}^{(z_{j})}$ in $B_{t}B_{\bar{t}}$ (4.19). The latter give rise to an integrand proportional to $d\big({z_{3}-{z_{1}+z_{2}\over 2}\over z_{12}}\big)\wedge d\log|{q_{1}\over q_{2}}|$ , which again vanishes upon subtracting divergent powers of $z_{12}$ . Combining this with (7.25), (7.26), we obtain the differential equation

$$ \displaystyle\xi^{\prime\prime}(x)+{\gamma}\xi(x)-2A(x)\xi^{\prime}(x)=0. $$

Using $A(x)=\phi^{\prime}(x)$ and ${1\over 2}|f(x)|^{2}=\phi^{\prime\prime}(x)$ from (7.15), we see that (7.29) is equivalent to

$$ \displaystyle\left(\partial_{x}^{2}+{\gamma}+{1\over 2}\right)\left(e^{-\phi(x)}\xi(x)\right)=0. $$

The behavior $\phi(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to\pm{\pi\over\sqrt{2}}$ suggests a Dirichlet type boundary condition for $e^{-\phi(x)}\xi(x)$ , with $\xi(x)$ itself behaving regularly at the boundary. An a priori justification of the latter requires going beyond the slow-varying field approximation analyzed thus far.

However, there is a natural interpretation of the boundary condition, as follows. In the $\lambda\to 0$ limit, the tachyon-dilaton profile of the background solution is negligible except near the pair of boundary walls $X\sim\pm{\pi\over\sqrt{2}\lambda}$ which are far separated. The central charge of the corresponding deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ (7.7) approaches 1. We propose that the deformed CFT describing each of the near-boundary regions in the $\lambda\to 0$ limit is the Runkel-Watts theory [35], which is an irrational unitarity CFT of central charge 1, and thus the full space can be viewed as sandwiched between a pair of “Runkel-Watts walls” (Figure 4).

The primaries $\phi_{p}$ of Runkel-Watts theory are labeled by a positive real parameter $p$ excluding positive integer values, with conformal weight $h_{p}=\widetilde{h}_{p}={p^{2}\over 4}$ .2020 20 The parameter $p$ of the primary $\phi_{p}$ is denoted $x$ in [35]. These are identified with the tachyon modes of momentum $p/\sqrt{2}$ that reflects off the wall, and missing primaries at positive integer $p$ are presumably due to resonance effects that result from interaction with the tachyon background. The structure constants $c(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ for a triple of primaries $\phi_{p_{1}},\phi_{p_{2}},\phi_{p_{3}}$ are given in [35]. As explained in Appendix A, a more natural basis of primaries is in fact $\phi_{p}^{\prime}=(-)^{\lfloor p\rfloor}\phi_{p}$ , where $\lfloor p\rfloor$ is the integer part of $p$ . Upon extension to negative $p$ by defining $\phi_{-p}=\phi_{p}$ , or equivalently $\phi^{\prime}_{-p}=-\phi_{p}^{\prime}$ , the Fourier transform of $\phi^{\prime}_{p}$ with respect to $p$ , denoted by $\widetilde{\phi}_{x}$ , has three-point function that behave in the large $x_{i}$ limit as2121 21 As the operators in question are dominated by primaries of weight close to zero, the (worldsheet) coordinate dependence of the three-function becomes negligible.

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{c}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\sim{\mathrm{c}onst}\cdot{\delta(x_{12})\delta(x_{13})\over x_{1}}. $$

This structure constant can be interpreted as the contact interaction of three tachyons at location $x$ ( $>0$ ) in the target space, with a spatially varying (string) coupling that diverges as $x\to 0$ , or equivalently a dilaton profile $\phi(x)\sim-\log x$ . This is in agreement with the near-boundary behavior of the SFT solution (7.19) at small $\lambda$ . Furthermore, the wave function of $\phi_{p}^{\prime}$ in $x$ -space is proportional to $\sin(px)$ , which in particular vanishes at $x=0$ . This wave function is to be identified with $e^{-\phi(x)}\xi(x)$ in (7.30) up to a shift of $x$ by $\pi\over\sqrt{2}$ , thereby justifying the proposal that $e^{-\phi(x)}\xi(x)$ should obey Dirichlet boundary condition.

The solutions to (7.30), subject to the boundary condition $e^{-\phi(x)}\xi(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\pm{\pi\over\sqrt{2}}$ , are

$$ \displaystyle\xi(x)={1\over\cos{x\over\sqrt{2}}}\sin{\ell(x+{\pi\over\sqrt{2}})\over\sqrt{2}},~~~~{\gamma}={1\over 2}(\ell^{2}-1),~~~\ell=1,2,\cdots $$

The corresponding scaling dimension of primaries in the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ is thus

$$ \displaystyle\Delta={1\over 2}\lambda^{2}(\ell^{2}-1)+{\cal O}(\lambda^{3}). $$

This is precisely in agreement with the spectrum of low-lying spectrum of the $A_{k}$ minimal model [7] at large $k$ , namely the $(r,s)$ degenerate primaries with $r=s=\ell$ , whose conformal weights are

$$ \displaystyle h_{\ell,\ell}=\widetilde{h}_{\ell,\ell}={\ell^{2}-1\over 4(k+2)(k+3)}, $$

provided the identification

$$ \displaystyle\lambda={1\over k}+{\cal O}(k^{-2}). $$

The latter is also such that the central charge of $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ (7.7) agrees with that of the minimal model, namely $c=1-{6\over(k+2)(k+3)}$ , up to ${\cal O}(\lambda^{3})$ corrections which we have not computed in SFT. Thus, we arrive at the inevitable and yet surprising conclusion that the deformed CFT $\mathbb{A}_{\lambda}$ is in fact the unitarity $A$ -series minimal model!

## 8 Discussion

In this paper we have formulated deformations of a 2D CFT in terms of solutions to the classical bosonic closed string field theory (SFT), and a strategy for extracting the deformed CFT data from the spectrum and amplitudes of on-shell fluctuations around the SFT solution. While the SFT formulation at first appears cumbersome due to the freedom in choosing the string vertices and the presence of $bc$ ghosts, these are in fact features that reveal the underlying structure of scheme dependence in Wilsonian renormalized conformal perturbation theory and the important role of the dilaton. The SFT approach is particularly suitable for dealing with noncompact CFTs whose the operator spectra are continuous and there are infinitely many nearly marginal deformations. As illustrated by the example of Horowitz-Polchinski solution, the naive conformal perturbation theory approach would involve marginal deformation operators that are singular in the target space, whereas the SFT deals directly with what amounts to the renormalized coupling or renormalized deformation operators, and produces regular solutions that reduces to those of the spacetime effective field theory in the slow-varying field approximation.

A particularly striking outcome of our analysis is the perturbatively-marginal $\cos(\sqrt{2}X)$ deformation of the noncompact free boson, which results in a condensation of tachyon and dilaton, and the emergence of the ends of space described by Runkel-Watts (RW) theory. While RW theory was originally discovered as the infinite $k$ limit of the $A_{k}$ minimal model, we find that the spectrum of minimal model can be recovered from the standing waves of tachyon between RW walls, up to higher order corrections to the identification of the deformation parameter $\lambda$ with $1/k$ . What we have not explained, however, is the quantization of the deformation parameter $\lambda$ intrinsically from the SFT perspective. This requires going beyond the slow-varying field approximation, and possibly understanding the convergence of perturbative closed SFT.

A slightly awkward feature of our SFT construction for CFT deformations that change the central charge is the necessity for introducing an extraneous linear dilaton “ $Y$ -sector”, and in principle having to fine tune the SFT solution that maintains the physical decoupling of this sector. An alternative possible approach is to construct an “off-critical SFT”, based on a worldsheet CFT with nonzero total central charge and BRST anomaly, where the zero string field is not a solution, while actual solutions to the SFT equation would recover the physics of a deformed and critical worldsheet CFT.

Conventional formulation of closed SFT requires rather complicated choice of string vertices that play the role of Feynman vertices and are by construction symmetric with respect to string fields. We have introduced a string field frame in which the string vertices are asymmetric, where one string field is viewed as outgoing and the rest incoming. This is particularly suitable for analyzing solutions to the SFT equation and fluctuations around the solution, as one can work in the “flat-vertex frame” in which the string bracket can be computed without applying nontrivial conformal transformations on the string fields. In the end, the string fields in the flat-vertex frame can be related to the string fields in a conventional frame by an in-principle known field redefinition. The technical simplification due to the flat-vertex frame has played an important role in simplify our analysis of SFT equations in the slow-varying field limit. It is of interest to systematize computations in the flat-vertex frame, which may facilitate practical implementation of higher order renormalized conformal perturbation theory and shed light on its convergence property.

Finally, we hope further analysis of string field solutions in the slow-varying field approximation will elucidate the nature of diffeomorphism in SFT [36], particularly concerning horizons in the spacetime, and clarify the meaning of the worldsheet CFT for time-dependent string backgrounds.

## Appendix A Runkel-Watts CFT data

The Runkel-Watts theory [35] is a $c=1$ irrational unitary CFT with primaries $\phi_{p}$ of conformal weight $h=\widetilde{h}={p^{2}\over 4}$ , where $p\in\mathbb{R}_{+}\backslash\mathbb{Z}_{+}$ . For convenience we will extend the parameter $p$ to negative real values by defining $\phi_{-p}=\phi_{p}$ . We further define $\phi^{\prime}_{p}\equiv(-)^{\lfloor p\rfloor}\phi_{p}$ , with $\phi^{\prime}_{-p}=-\phi^{\prime}(p)$ . As such the two-point functions are normalized according to

$$ \displaystyle\left\langle\phi^{\prime}_{p_{1}}(z_{1})\phi^{\prime}_{p_{2}}(0)\right\rangle=\left(\delta(p_{1}-p_{2})-\delta(p_{1}+p_{2})\right)|z|^{-p_{1}^{2}}, $$

and the three-point functions take the form

$$ \displaystyle\left\langle\phi^{\prime}_{p_{1}}(z_{1})\phi^{\prime}_{p_{2}}(z_{2})\phi^{\prime}_{p_{3}}(z_{3})\right\rangle={c^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})\over|z_{12}|^{p_{1}^{2}+p_{2}^{2}-p_{3}^{2}\over 2}|z_{23}|^{p_{2}^{2}+p_{3}^{2}-p_{1}^{2}\over 2}|z_{13}|^{p_{1}^{2}+p_{3}^{2}-p_{2}^{2}\over 2}}. $$

The structure constant $c^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ is given by

$$ \displaystyle c^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})=P^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})e^{Q(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})}, $$

where $Q$ is given in equation (10) of [35], and $P^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ is related to the function $P(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ defined in equation (9) of [35] by the sign $(-)^{\lfloor p_{1}\rfloor+\lfloor p_{2}\rfloor+\lfloor p_{3}\rfloor}$ and the aforementioned extension to negative values of $p_{i}$ . The sign change in our choice of basis is such that $P^{\prime\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ can be expressed as

$$ \displaystyle P^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3}) \displaystyle={1\over 2}\big(\Theta(p_{1}+p_{2}-p_{3})+\Theta(p_{1}+p_{3}-p_{2})+\Theta(p_{2}+p_{3}-p_{1})+\Theta(-p_{1}-p_{2}-p_{3})-2\big) \displaystyle-{1\over 2}\sum_{\epsilon_{i}=\pm}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\epsilon_{1}\epsilon_{2}\epsilon_{3}\Theta(\epsilon_{1}p_{1}+\epsilon_{2}p_{2}+\epsilon_{3}p_{3}-2n), $$

where $\Theta$ is the Heaviside step function.

The function $Q$ is defined as the analytic continuation of

$$ \displaystyle Q(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{d\beta}{(-\log\beta)(1-\beta)^{2}}R(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3},\beta) $$

from the domain $0<p_{i}<1$ , $p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}<2$ , where $R$ is defined as

$$ \displaystyle R(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3},\beta)=2+\sum_{\epsilon=\pm}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\beta^{\epsilon p_{i}}-\sum_{\epsilon_{i}=\pm}\beta^{{1\over 2}\left(\epsilon_{1}p_{1}+\epsilon_{2}p_{2}+\epsilon_{3}p_{3}\right)}. $$

Note that near $\beta=1$ , $R$ has a fourth order zero whereas the denominator in the integrand of (A.5) has a third order zero, and the integral is convergent. To analyze the properties of $Q$ , it useful to write the RHS of (A.5) as

$$ \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}d\beta\int_{0}^{\infty}du\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n\beta^{u+n-1}R(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3},\beta). $$

The absolute convergence of the summation and integration allows for swapping their order, giving

$$ \displaystyle Q(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3}) \displaystyle=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n\int_{0}^{\infty}du\int_{0}^{1}d\beta\beta^{u+n-1}R(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3},\beta) \displaystyle=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n\int_{0}^{\infty}du\left(\frac{2}{u+n}+\sum_{\epsilon=\pm}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\frac{1}{u+n+\epsilon p_{i}}-\sum_{\epsilon_{i}=\pm}\frac{1}{u+n+{1\over 2}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\epsilon_{i}p_{i}}\right) \displaystyle=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n\left(-2\log n-\sum_{\epsilon=\pm}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\log(n+\epsilon p_{i})+\sum_{\epsilon_{i}=\pm}\log\big(n+{1\over 2}\sum_{i=1}^{3}\epsilon_{i}p_{i}\big)\right). $$

In particular, note that in the limit of simultaneously scaling $p_{1},p_{2},p_{3}$ to 0, $Q$ vanishes at quartic order. We further observe that $e^{Q}$ has a pole of order $|n|$ when any one of $p_{1},p_{2},p_{3}$ takes an integer value $n$ , and a zero of order $n$ when $\sum_{i=1}^{3}\epsilon_{i}p_{i}=2n$ for some positive integer $n$ and $\epsilon_{i}=\pm$ . One can verify that when $P^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ is nonzero, $e^{Q(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})}$ remains finite.

Now we pass to the target position space by Fourier transforming the basis of primaries $\phi_{p}^{\prime}$ with respect to $p$ , and consider

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{\phi}_{x}\equiv\int dp\,e^{ipx}\phi^{\prime}_{p}. $$

While $\widetilde{\phi}_{x}$ does not have a definite conformal weight, we are particularly interested in the large $x$ limit where the small weight component dominates and the coordinate dependence of correlation functions can be ignored, so that the three-point function of $\widetilde{\phi}_{x}$ can be expressed as

$$ \displaystyle\widetilde{c}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})\approx\int{dp_{1}dp_{2}dp_{3}}e^{ip_{1}x_{1}+ip_{2}x_{2}+ip_{3}x_{3}}c^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3}). $$

Furthermore, the large distance behavior of $\widetilde{c}$ is controlled by the momentum space discontinuity of $c^{\prime}$ , particularly along the $\pm p_{1}\pm p_{2}\pm p_{3}=0$ planes. Near $p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}=0$ , for instance, where $Q(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ vanishes, the discontinuity in $c^{\prime}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})$ is captured by

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}\Theta(p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}). $$

Taking its Fourier transform gives the contribution to $\widetilde{c}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})$ ,

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}\int{dp_{1}dp_{2}dp_{3}}\left(\frac{1}{ix_{1}}\partial_{p_{1}}e^{ip_{1}x_{1}+ip_{2}x_{2}+ip_{3}x_{3}}\right)\Theta(p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3})=-\frac{i}{2x_{1}}(2\pi)^{2}\delta(x_{12})\delta(x_{13}). $$

## Abstract

We study $U(N)$ Chern-Simons theory coupled to massive fundamental fermions in the lightcone Hamiltonian formalism. Focusing on the planar limit, we introduce a consistent regularization scheme, identify the counter terms needed to restore relativistic invariance, and formulate scattering theory in terms of unambiguously defined asymptotic states. We determine the $2\to 2$ planar S-matrix element in the singlet channel by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation to all orders, establishing a result previously conjectured in the literature.
